evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep said: 'We'll start with few questions to get you on the right track. That should take about five to ten minutes of your time. Then you'll be able to build an accurate code which should, which you can depend on. Sounds good.' — framed the time and promise, but no explicit wait for confirmation, moved straight ahead.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Mary Breindel), moving date (October 23rd), city-to-city (Fort Worth to Dallas area, 4900 Gauge Avenue), apartment size (~700 sq ft, one bedroom) — all four covered.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asked 'And do you have any concerns or any important things that you wanted to answer during this call today?' — but this came after already collecting current address, zip code, floor info, and beginning logistics probing. Should have asked before any of that.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer said 'Contract' as a concern. Rep said 'No, we'll kind of just go through the process and see what we can do.' No follow-up, no 'tell me more about that,' call moved directly to contact collection.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection offered. Rep acknowledged the contract concern but did not reflect back or confirm what was heard.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment), floor/stories (3rd floor current, 2nd floor new), access (both stairs and elevators), walking distance (100 feet), special items (2 TVs, 2 dressers, marble coffee table), all covered. Box count range provided (15-35 boxes for typical one-bedroom).
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep asked 'And no need help in packing this is from point eight point B.' — unclear phrasing, no clean offer of packing services.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep said 'And a typical back count based on one bedroom appointment would be between fifteen to 35 boxes. Do you feel that you fall within that range?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provided typical range: 'a typical one bedroom apartment normally takes two movers. That's between two and a half to three and a half hours to complete' and personalized: 'In your case, we're coming from a one bedroom apartment located on the third floor with elevators going to the new location which is also a one bedroom apartment located on the second floor. So, we'll send out two movers and one truck estimated time is between three to four hours estimated cost in case they end up four hours would be $974.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep disclosed: hourly rate ($103/hour per mover), trip fee ($150), minimum (2.5 hours), increment (15 minutes), all included items (gas, truck, wraps, tools, disassembly/reassembly), and trip-fee boundary (10–15 mile free zone). Full transparency provided.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or any equivalent. Moved directly into Two Promises section without pausing for customer reaction to the price.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep said: 'We have on time guarantee we value your time. So, if you cannot make it to the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.' — discount terms clearly stated.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep said: 'We have no worry damage coverage included on the already weight that you're paying us. We will provide up to 2000 dollars per move. That is the repair, replace and reimburse for your items.' — coverage amount and 'included' (not add-on) stated, but no explicit 'no deductible / no fine print' framing.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No closing question like 'Does that put those to rest?' after Two Promises. Rep moved directly to logistics (booking date/time).
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep never asked 'What's still concerning you?' or any genuine version. Went straight to offer to email the quote.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep did not ask 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' Customer volunteered 'Are you all able to, to email me this quote?' and rep said 'Yeah, sure I can, so, in case if you decide to book with us...' — offers email but no direct ask to book.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep said: 'There's no deposit required, no risk and securing your spot. So in case if you wanted to reschedule or to cancel then all you have to do is just simply give us a call at anytime.' — no-deposit confirmed, implying rate lock, though not explicitly labeled.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep confirmed: date (October 23rd, Friday), time window (8:30–9:00 AM), no deposit, and email address (braindel.mary@gmail.com). Missing: phone number confirmation (though provided earlier in call), arrival window detail, crew size (mentioned 2 movers earlier but not re-confirmed at close), and no notes left for crew about concerns (contract concern never fully resolved or documented).

top_strength: Zhang gathered comprehensive logistics details across both apartments (floors, elevator/stair access, walking distance, special items, floor layout) and delivered full pricing transparency with hourly rate, trip fee, minimums, and inclusions clearly stated upfront.
coaching_note: Never asked the critical closing question 'Would you like our help with your move?' — customer interest remained unconfirmed, and the contract concern raised at the start was never circled back to or resolved before the call ended.
